title: Blower Motor Removal and Refitting
introduction:
The blower motor supplies the cabin’s moving air; other climate-control components handle heating and cooling. I keep that distinction in mind before taking anything apart: a new air mover cannot, by itself, explain an air-temperature complaint.

Access begins at the right-hand insulation panel and its ambient light. The next drawing shows the harness crossing the blower like a seat belt across a parcel—release the belt before trying to remove the parcel. I finish the removal and refit with a normal fan-speed check. Airflow that responds to your controls is a useful finish line; it does not prove that every heating or cooling fault has vanished.

items.name: Disable remote start
items.detail: Before service around the vehicle, disable remote start, if equipped, through the Central Display: Vehicle settings > Remote Start Setup. Otherwise, the vehicle could be remotely started during service, causing personal injury or death.

items.name: Remove the key
items.detail: Switch the ignition OFF and remove the key from the vehicle to prevent another person from starting the engine during service. An accidental start can cause serious personal injury.

items.name: Eyes, ears and hands
items.detail: Wear eye and ear protection during vehicle service, and protective gloves when handling pointed or sharp-edged components. Failure to use this protection may result in serious personal injury.

items.name: Review the system precautions
items.detail: Before starting, read [Climate Control System Health and Safety Precautions](#/document/G1693184), as required by the general service warnings. The illustrated blower operation involves the insulation panel, ambient light, wiring and motor attachments; it calls for no refrigerant or heater-water-hose disconnection.

items.name: Use the drawings to distinguish the attachments
items.detail: Identify the insulation-panel push pins and ambient-light fitting in the panel illustration. In the motor illustration, distinguish the wiring harness retainers from the motor retainers and identify the electrical connector. Keep these attachment groups separate in your understanding of the removal order.

items.name: Park before working
items.detail: Park the vehicle and apply the parking brake before starting footwell work. Keep the vehicle stationary throughout the repair and completion check.

edits.text: Remove the push pins, then lower the right-hand (RH) insulation panel for removal, releasing its ambient light as described below.
edits.why: The panel illustration highlights the panel in blue and its push pins in magenta; the downward arrow shows the panel’s removal direction. Lowering the panel exposes its attached ambient light, which must be freed before the panel can be taken clear.

edits.text: Release and remove the insulation panel ambient light from the panel as shown in the inset.
edits.why: Viewed from the exposed underside of the insulation panel, turn the ambient-light fitting counterclockwise to release it, then withdraw it from the opening. Support the panel until the fitting is free so its weight does not pull on the light wiring.

edits.text: Disconnect the blower motor electrical connector. Release the wiring harness retainers and move the harness aside. Then remove the blower motor retainers and remove the motor.
edits.why: The motor drawing highlights the target in blue, the harness to move aside in yellow, and the attachment points in magenta. Its separate callouts distinguish the harness retainers from the motor retainers. I clear the harness first so it no longer crosses the part being removed; unclipping wiring and unfastening the motor are different jobs.

edits.text: Reverse the removal sequence: refit the blower motor and its retainers, return the wiring harness to its illustrated route and reattach its retainers, then reconnect the blower motor connector. Refit the ambient light to the insulation panel, position the panel and reinstall its push pins.
edits.why:
To secure the ambient-light fitting during refitting, insert it into the panel opening and turn it clockwise when viewed from the exposed underside. Refitting is complete when the motor is secured, its connector is reconnected, the harness is back in its retainers, and the light and panel are restored. I compare the harness with the motor drawing before closing the panel, while its route is still visible.

With the panel fully restored, remove tools and clear your hands from the blower and wiring. Keep the car parked with the parking brake applied, then switch the ignition on for a normal control check. With Electronic Manual Temperature Control (EMTC), vary the blower switch and confirm airflow changes. With Dual Automatic Temperature Control (DATC), use the blower override buttons to select different speeds. See the [EMTC controls](#/document/G1681091) and [DATC controls](#/document/G1676851). This checks the installed blower, not every climate-control function. If airflow does not respond, switch the ignition off and remove the key before checking the connections disturbed during this job. If those are secure and the complaint remains, return to climate-control diagnosis. No parts-cannon bullshit just because the fan is being stubborn. After a successful check, switch the ignition off and remove the key.
